items.title: Prompt caching se AI ka jawab badal jata hai? Aur lambi chat idle chhodo to?
items.one_idea: Prompt caching only reuses the already-processed prompt prefix and never changes the answer; Claude Code now also compacts a very long idle chat before its one-hour cache expires so your next message does not reprocess everything.
items.spoken_hook: Prompt caching se AI ka jawab badal jata hai?
items.hook_10s: AI interview mein pucha: caching se AI ka jawab badal jata hai? Nahi, jawab bilkul same rehta hai. Isme teen baatein hain. [frame 0: two identical answer bubbles joined by an equals sign]
items.visual_idea: A prompt block is stamped 'processed' and kept in a box with a ticking clock; two answer bubbles with and without the box come out identical; near the end of the clock a long chat shrinks to a short card before the box closes.
items.everyday_anchor: You wait for a lift and the same chai order is remembered by the cafe so it is made faster, but it tastes the same.
items.example: Label example: a 200K token chat idle ~54 minutes gets compacted (release note); cache read 0.1x, 5-min write 1.25x (docs).
facts_to_verify: v2.1.299 (14 Oct 2026): 200K+ token chat idle ~54 min is compacted before its one-hour cache expires
Caching has no effect on output generation; response is identical
cache read 0.1x, 5-minute write 1.25x, default 5-min lifetime
Idle compaction is stated for the terminal (Claude Code CLI) only
items.cover_headline: Does prompt caching change the answer?
items.notes: Caveats: idle compaction is documented for the terminal only, do not generalize; release note says 54 min vs a one-hour cache while docs say default cache is 5 min (the 1-hour option is the one in play), explain or leave out; no savings percentage in sources, never claim one; do not say 'new' for caching itself. hook_type misconception_question is NOT yet allowed by validate_queue.py (see state/proposals/2026-10-17-misconception-question.md); validation fails on e101 until the owner approves.

items.title: Safety check crash hua, phir bhi AI ka kaam ho gaya: ab fail hone par block karo
items.one_idea: A Claude Code hook is a small check that runs around an agent's action; with onFailure block, a check that crashes, times out or exits oddly now stops the action instead of letting it through (fail closed, not fail open).
items.spoken_hook: Guard crash हुआ, फिर भी agent ने काम कर दिया।
items.hook_10s: Guard crash hua, phir bhi agent ne kaam kar diya. Aisa kyun hota hai? Teen halaat mein ab action rukta hai. [frame 0: a red cross on the guard while the door stays open]
items.visual_idea: Before/after of a door: guard check crashes and the door swings open; with onFailure block the same crash keeps the door locked.
items.everyday_anchor: A UPI app's fraud check is down: should payments go through anyway or wait?
items.example: Label example: a check that times out. No real numbers needed.
facts_to_verify: v2.1.295 (8 Oct 2026) added onFailure: block for command and HTTP hooks
a hook that cannot start, times out or exits with an unexpected code blocks the action instead of letting it through
items.cover_headline: When the safety check crashes, block
items.notes: Caveats: vendor release note and docs only; advanced for beginners, so define 'hook' in one plain sentence; read the single-release page https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/releases/tag/v2.1.295 again before scripting.

items.title: Ek line likho, agent poori machine ka exploded drawing bana de: anatomy skill

items.visual_idea: A one-line prompt on the left; on the right a rate limiter pulls apart into labelled parts that float apart in an exploded view.
items.everyday_anchor: A mechanic's exploded parts diagram that finally shows how a gearbox fits together.

items.title: Context mein kya-kya jata hai? Context ke 5 sources
items.one_idea: The context is everything the model sees when it answers: system prompt, tools, examples, message history and external data, and each source should stay lean.
items.spoken_hook: Model ko jawab dene se pehle kya-kya dikhta hai?
items.hook_10s: Model ko jawab dene se pehle kya-kya dikhta hai? Ek window mein paanch cheezein. Aaj paanchon samajhte hain. [frame 0: an empty window frame with five labelled boxes outside]
items.visual_idea: Five boxes (system prompt, tools, examples, history, outside data) slide into one window frame and fill it up.
items.everyday_anchor: Packing a school bag: only five things go in and the bag has limited space.
items.example: Label example: a support chatbot with a system prompt, a tool and a chat history.
facts_to_verify: context sources: system prompts, tools, examples, message history, external data
bloated tool sets and long histories are common failures; context is a finite resource
items.cover_headline: What goes into an AI's context?
items.notes: Caveat: Anthropic engineering post is guidance, not a measurement; q03 and q15 already cover the context window idea, keep this reel about the five sources.

items.title: Context compaction kya hai? Lambi chat ko chhota kaise karte hain
items.one_idea: Compaction summarises a conversation that is nearing the window limit and restarts a new window with the summary, while low-risk pruning drops redundant tool outputs.
items.hook_10s: Context compaction kya hota hai? Lambi chat ko summary banakar chhota karna. Teen steps. [frame 0: a full window bar shrinking to a small summary card]
items.visual_idea: A filling window bar hits the limit, folds into a short summary card, and a fresh window opens holding only that card.
items.everyday_anchor: Packing a long WhatsApp group chat into a three-line summary for someone who just joined.
items.example: Label example: a 30-message chat compressed to a short summary.
facts_to_verify: compaction: summarising contents and reinitiating a new context window with the summary
low-risk pruning: discarding redundant tool outputs or messages
as context grows recall decreases (context rot)
items.cover_headline: How does an AI shrink a long chat?
keywords: long chat context kaise manage kare
items.notes: Caveat: angle differs from q16 (sliding window, vector DB); summary can lose details, say so.

items.title: RAG kya hai? AI ko apni notebook dekhne do
items.one_idea: RAG retrieves relevant information from a knowledge base and adds it to the user's prompt, so the model answers from your documents.
items.hook_10s: RAG kya hai? AI jawab dene se pehle apni notebook se sahi pages nikalta hai. Teen steps. [frame 0: a question beside a shelf of notebook pages]
items.visual_idea: A question goes to a shelf of pages, the three closest pages light up, slide into the prompt box and then the answer appears.
items.everyday_anchor: Looking up the right page in your notes before answering an exam question.
items.example: Label example: a company handbook split into pages.
facts_to_verify: RAG pairs a pretrained language model with an external retrieval component (Lewis et al.)
RAG retrieves relevant information from a knowledge base and appends it to the user's prompt
chunks turned into embeddings; most similar retrieved at runtime
items.notes: Caveat: q05/q17/q20 already cover RAG trade-offs and failures; this reel is the plain definition. The paper abstract does not measure provenance or knowledge updates, do not claim it did.

items.title: Interview: Poora PDF context mein daal doon ya RAG banaun?
items.one_idea: If a knowledge base is under about 200,000 tokens you can put all of it in the prompt (with prompt caching); above that you retrieve chunks with RAG.
items.spoken_hook: 40 page का handbook, और उसने RAG बना दिया।
items.hook_10s: 40 page ka handbook, aur usne RAG bana diya. Use RAG ki zaroorat hi nahi thi. Interview mein yahi poocha jata hai. Teen rules. [frame 0: a small handbook beside a huge machine]
items.visual_idea: A small stack of pages drops straight into the prompt box; a huge library will not fit and goes through a retrieval funnel instead.
items.everyday_anchor: Carrying a thin notebook in your bag versus renting a whole library to read one chapter.
items.example: Label example: a 40-page handbook (illustrative, not a measured number).
facts_to_verify: under 200,000 tokens you can include the whole knowledge base in the prompt, RAG not needed
prompt caching cuts latency by more than 2x and costs by up to 90% (Anthropic's own figures)
items.cover_headline: Whole PDF in prompt or RAG?
keywords: pdf prompt mein daalna ya rag
items.notes: Caveat: 200,000-token figure and caching savings are Anthropic's own; the 40-page handbook is an illustration, say 'maan lo'. Not a repeat of q03 (context rot) or q05 (RAG vs fine-tuning).

items.title: Interview: Agent loop mein fas gaya, ye kaise rokoge? (Onit job post)
items.one_idea: An agent needs stopping conditions such as a maximum number of iterations, ground truth from the environment at each step and human checkpoints.
items.spoken_hook: Onit के AI Engineer job post में agent loops हैं। Loop में फँस जाए, तो कैसे रोकोगे?
items.hook_10s: Onit ke AI Engineer job post mein agent loops hain. Loop mein phans jaye, to kaise rokoge? Jawab teen rules mein hai. [frame 0: a looping arrow with a counter and a stop sign]
items.visual_idea: An agent circle repeats with a step counter; at the max count a stop sign cuts the loop and a human-check gate opens.
items.everyday_anchor: A phone app stuck on a spinner that never ends until you force-close it.
facts_to_verify: Onit AI Engineer job post (Pune) asks for experience with agent loops, tool interfaces, planning/replanning, memory/state and failure handling
stopping conditions such as a maximum number of iterations; ground truth from the environment at each step; pause for human feedback at checkpoints
items.cover_headline: How do you stop a looping AI agent?
items.notes: Caveats: Onit page is a JOB POST, not an interview question and has no posting date and no About section: say 'job post', never 'interview mein pucha'; confirm company name on the Lever page before showing it; page never mentions stop conditions, those come from Anthropic's building-effective-agents post (guidance, gives no specific limit).

items.title: Interview: Chatbot ne galat jawab diya, pata kaise chalega kyun?
items.one_idea: A trace records one request as nested spans, each with a name, start and end time, so you can see which step (retrieval, prompt, tool) went wrong or slow.
items.spoken_hook: Interviewer ने पूछा: Production chatbot ne galat jawab diya, tumhe kaise pata chalega kyun?
items.hook_10s: Interviewer ne poocha: production chatbot ne galat jawab diya, tumhe kaise pata chalega kyun? Sirf final jawab dekhna kaafi nahi. Trace chahiye. Teen cheezein. [frame 0: a wrong answer bubble with a question mark]
items.visual_idea: One request drawn as a row of nested bars (retrieve, prompt, tool, answer); the bad step lights red so you see exactly where it broke.
items.everyday_anchor: A courier tracking page that shows every stop, so you know where the parcel got stuck.
items.example: Label example: retrieve, prompt, tool, answer as four spans.
facts_to_verify: a trace shows the full path of a request
a span is one unit of work with name, start and end times and attributes
parent span IDs form a hierarchy
items.cover_headline: How do you debug a wrong AI answer?
items.notes: Caveat: OpenTelemetry page defines tracing in general; the LLM-specific mapping (retrieval, prompt, tool as spans) is our illustration, label it as an example. Onit job post (https://jobs.lever.co/onit/5110cadf-965f-4597-ae95-7d4c000675d7) lists tracing but is not used as company hook here.

items.title: Interview: Chatbot ne galat jawab diya, par kal ka kuch record nahi. Debug kaise karoge?
items.one_idea: When an LLM app gives a wrong answer, the final answer alone cannot tell you why; a trace, one record of the whole request with each step's input, output, time and tokens, shows which step went wrong.
items.spoken_hook: Interviewer ने पूछा: AI app ने गलत जवाब दिया, तो आप कैसे पता लगाओगे कि गलती कहाँ हुई?
items.hook_10s: Interviewer ने पूछा: AI app ने गलत जवाब दिया, तो आप कैसे पता लगाओगे कि गलती कहाँ हुई? ज़्यादातर लोग सिर्फ़ आख़िरी जवाब देखते हैं। Interview में यही पकड़ा जाता है। इसकी तीन बातें हैं. [chat bubble with a wrong answer and a red cross]

hook_candidates.text: Interviewer ने पूछा: AI app ने गलत जवाब दिया, तो आप कैसे पता लगाओगे कि गलती कहाँ हुई?
Chatbot ने गलत जवाब दिया, और log में सिर्फ़ वही जवाब है। अब गलती कहाँ ढूँढोगे?
Parcel टूटकर आया, तो tracking से पता चलता है कि कहाँ टूटा। AI app में ये कैसे करोगे?

items.visual_idea: A request travels as a line of boxes: question, search, tool call, model, answer. Each box shows a small timer and token count. The wrong answer is traced back, one box (the search) turns red while the others stay green.
items.everyday_anchor: A courier parcel arrives damaged and the tracking page shows which hub dropped it, so you do not guess.
items.example: Labelled example: a refund chatbot answers 30 days, the trace shows the search step returned an old policy page.
facts_to_verify: A trace is a structured record of one request's lifecycle (LLM calls, retrieval steps, tool executions) with timing, inputs, outputs and metadata (Langfuse docs, a vendor definition; say 'tracing' as common practice, no numbers).
items.cover_headline: Wrong AI answer? Trace every step

items.title: Chhota jawab padhne se bill kam hota hai? cc-stretch: click karo, jawab khulta hai
items.one_idea: cc-stretch is a Claude Code plugin that shows short replies where each linked phrase expands in place when clicked; you read less, but by the author's own statement you do not pay less, because each reply costs about the same tokens.
items.spoken_hook: Jawab chhota padho, to kya bill bhi kam hoga?
items.hook_10s: Jawab chhota padho, to kya bill bhi kam hoga? Nahi, bill wahi rehta hai. Par padhna bahut kam. Ek plugin, teen baatein. [frame 0: a long reply collapsing into a short card, a price tag staying the same]
items.visual_idea: A long wall of reply text folds into one short card with a few underlined phrases; a click on a phrase opens a small box in place and a click on the arrow closes it, while a price tag beside it stays the same.
items.everyday_anchor: A newspaper front page shows headlines and you open only the story you care about, though the whole paper was still printed.
items.example: Label example: a long answer about a bug shown as three short lines with two clickable phrases. The author's own measure: default view was 17% of the words over 69 replies from four projects.
facts_to_verify: repo created 2026-10-14, MIT license, not affiliated with Anthropic
install: /plugin install cc-stretch --marketplace pro-vi/cc-stretch, then /tui fullscreen (clicks need fullscreen terminal)
author claim: default view was 17% of the words over 69 replies from 4 projects; about two of three key points visible (author's own numbers)
author states: you read less, you do not pay less (similar token cost)
uses an early-access plugin API that changes between releases; Windows clicks reportedly not working yet
items.cover_headline: Short replies that open when you click
keywords: ai ka jawab chhota kaise padhein
items.notes: Caveats: all numbers are the author's own measure on his own replies, say 'author says'; never show a star count; plugin is early access and Claude Code only; do not claim savings in tokens or money (the page says none). Chosen over AirsupHQ/machine-skill (https://github.com/AirsupHQ/machine-skill, 296 stars, one-line to 3D simulation) because e103 anatomy skill is the same picture (one line to exploded diagram); machine-skill is the backup. Researcher-verified; facts re-fetched by the strategist 2026-10-18.

items.title: Model pichli chat kyun bhool jata hai? AI ki memory notebook
items.one_idea: The context window is a small, limited desk that gets cluttered as it fills; agent memory means writing notes to storage outside the window and reading them back when needed, and the memory tool is that notebook: a /memories folder your own app manages.
items.spoken_hook: Model pichli chat kyun bhool jata hai?
items.hook_10s: Model pichli chat kyun bhool jata hai? Kyunki uski desk chhoti hai. Notebook se yaad rakhta hai. Teen steps. [frame 0: a small desk crowded with papers beside an empty notebook]
items.visual_idea: A small desk fills with papers until it overflows; the model writes a note into a notebook shelf outside the desk, the desk is cleared, and a later question pulls the same note back onto the clean desk.
items.everyday_anchor: You note an exam formula in your copy so you can clear your desk and find it again tomorrow.
items.example: Label example: a coding agent writes 'user prefers Python, project uses pytest' to a notes file and reads it next session.
facts_to_verify: context is a finite resource; Anthropic names context rot as tokens grow (engineering post)
structured note-taking: the agent writes notes persisted outside the context window and pulls them back later (engineering post)
memory tool: client-side, a /memories directory your application manages; the model issues file commands, your app executes them (docs)
MemGPT abstract: manages memory tiers to give the appearance of extended context
items.cover_headline: Why AI forgets and how memory fixes it
items.notes: Caveats: r101/r102 and q15/q16 cover the context window and compaction; this reel is only about notes kept outside the window. Memory tool is Anthropic-specific and client-side: say 'for example'; do not say the model stores it itself. Do not claim MemGPT numbers. Unit D6.
